newsitem.title: FRANCE: BOBSLEIGH-WIESE PILOTS GERMANY TO SECOND WIN.
newsitem.headline: BOBSLEIGH-WIESE PILOTS GERMANY TO SECOND WIN.

text.p: Dirk Wiese piloted his bobsled to victory on Sunday as Germany continued their early season domination of the World Cup four-man competition.
It was the second consecutive win for the Germans after Harald Czudai led a sweep of the top three places at the opening four-man event of the season last weekend on home ice in Altenberg, Germany.

Wiese produced two consistent runs. He posted the third quickest time on his first run down the 1992 Olympic layout then came back with the second fastest on a deteriorating track in his second trip to finish with an aggregate time of one minute, 56.16 seconds.
Marcel Rohner used a brilliant second run to climb from eighth to second and propel Switzerland onto the podium for the first time this season with a clocking of 1:56.33.
Gunther Huber, who piloted Italy to a third place in Saturday's two-man competition, was third once again in 1:56.37.
Reto Gotschi gave Switzerland two sleds in the top five after he crossed fourth in 1:56.51.

The sledders were back on the track just 12 hours after the two-man competition. The four-man event was run in near ideal weather unlike the blizzard conditions that plagued Saturday's race and caused a seven hour delay.
